newsitem.title: USA: Marvel settlement still in flux.
newsitem.headline: Marvel settlement still in flux.

text.p: A bankruptcy judge Friday said Marvel Entertainment Group Inc could continue to use cash collateral while it works out differences in a recent settlement proposal with its banks, creditors and the bondholders of the parent company, Marvel Holdings Inc.
An attorney close to the case told Reuters Judge Helen Balick of the U.S. Bankruptcy Court in Delaware scheduled a status hearing on Friday for August 20.

At that time, she will consider the banks' motion for a court-appointed trustee unless a settlement has been reached by then among Marvel, its proposed merger partner Toy Biz Inc, the pre-petition lenders led by Chase Manhattan Bank and bondholders led by investor Carl Icahn.

A court-appointed trustee would manage the assets of Marvel's estate, taking over that responsibility from the Marvel board of Icahn-appointed directors, which is the debtor- in-possession trustee. The bank group, which has a $705 million secured claim, wants an independent trustee to oversee the assets to insure repayment of the loans.

"As time goes by, the business (of Marvel Entertainment) is eroding," the source said. "The banks want to know how their payback will actually be implemented before they are willing to let a new lender be granted liens ahead of them."
At issue is a provision in the settlement proposal for new $150 million debtor-in-possession financing for Marvel from two Icahn-controlled subsidiaries.

"We're attempting to settle all open issues, but the negotiaions are taking place in the context of those potential battles" over whether new loans can leapfrog in priority over existing ones, the source said.
The source said that, if the settlement issues can be resolved by August 20 and a plan of reorganization drafted thereafter, Marvel could possibly emerge from bankruptcy by year end.
On Tuesday Balick will consider a motion to approve direct bank financing for Marvel subsidiary Panini SpA, which, under the settlement, is to be spun-off to the Chase bank lenders.
